name: Rosewood Munich
positioning: City hotel in Munich's old town, set in a 1703 palais and a former State Bank of Bavaria headquarters from 1894
best_for: Travelers who want a base in the middle of Munich's old town
Guests who enjoy live jazz and cocktails in the evening
Families or groups who want to stay together in combined rooms and suites

facts.text: The hotel is in the middle of Munich's old town, the Altstadt.
The interiors preserve original elements such as the grand staircase and Baroque frescoes in the lobby.
The interiors were reimagined by local architects Hilmer Sattler Architekten Ahlers Albrecht.
Rooms feature whimsical artwork by German illustrator Olaf Hajek.
Brasserie Cuvillies serves refined, seasonal Bavarian dishes crafted from local ingredients.
Brasserie Cuvillies is named after the architect of the Palais that forms part of the hotel.
The light-flooded Wintergarten serves breakfasts and afternoon teas from pastry chef Shinas Shahida, and has a fireplace.
Bar Montez has a piano and wood-paneled walls with a cozy, library-like feel.
Bar Montez has live jazz every night.
The private dining room at Brasserie Cuvillies seats up to 14 guests, directly beside the main restaurant.
Kids can join cooking and arts and crafts classes, and babysitters are available on demand.
The hotel offers a private tour of the Nymphenburg Porcelain Manufactory.

highlights.text: The hotel comprises two historic buildings: the Palais Neuhaus-Preysing from 1703 and the former State Bank of Bavaria headquarters built in 1894.
Bar Montez serves signature cocktails and snacks with live jazz and pays homage to Lola Montez, muse of King Ludwig I of Bavaria.
Palaishof is an open-air dining spot set within a secluded inner courtyard.
The Houses offer one to four bedroom layouts with services such as butler care, flexible arrivals and private wellness sessions.
The Asaya spa has an indoor pool, two saunas and an herbal steam bath.

considerations.text: The spa pool is indoors; the hotel sits in the middle of Munich's old town.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the hotel's high-end positioning.
WhataHotel notes availability can be limited.
